Pillar 1: Clinical Problem Statement

Why Manual Polysomnography Scoring Is Broken

The Clinical Reality:

  • • Massive Patient Need: Over 936 million adults suffer from Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) and insomnia worldwide.
  • • The Gold Standard Test: Overnight Polysomnography (PSG) in an in-hospital sleep lab with 20+ sensor wires monitoring brain, eyes, muscles, heart, and breathing.
  • • The 30s Epoch Standard: An 8-hour recording produces nearly 1,000 thirty-second slices ("epochs") that must each be scored into Wake, N1, N2, N3, or REM.
  • • Human Exhaustion: Certified sleep technologists must visually inspect every single 30s epoch for 1.5 to 3 hours per patient!
  • • Subjectivity Ceiling: Human agreement is only ~75% (kappa ~ 0.70-0.76). Humans disagree on 1 out of 4 epochs.
  • • Consequences: Severe 6 to 12-month patient waitlists, $1,500-$3,000 per study, and high misdiagnosis risk.
Clinical Bottleneck: Manual Review Unsustainable
Pillar 2: Existing Approaches & Pitfalls

How It Is Generally Solved: 3 Critical Pitfalls

Pitfall A

Single-Signal Blindness

Commercial headbands or smartwatches try to stage sleep using only 1 EEG channel or optical pulse photoplethysmography (PPG).

Why it fails: Cannot detect muscle paralysis during REM or paradoxical chest effort during apnea. Misclassifies quiet wakefulness as deep sleep.
Clinically Incomplete
Pitfall B

Black-Box Neural Overfitting

End-to-end heavy deep learning architectures (e.g. 200,000+ parameter BiGRUs or heavy LSTMs) trained directly on raw noisy signals.

Why it fails: Severe memorization of lab-specific noise. In our benchmarks, raw BiGRU collapsed to 18.8% F1 under cross-patient evaluation.
Collapses on New Patients
Pitfall C

Destructive Inner-Join Filtering

Traditional pipelines throw away an entire 30s epoch if even one channel has movement or sensor noise (e.g. slipped nasal cannula).

Why it fails: Discards 20% to 40% of patient data! For patient SN2, 40.7% of clean brain data was thrown in the trash.
Massive Data Loss
Pillar 3: Our Proposed Solution

Our Proposed Architecture: Multimodal Synergy & Clinical Rules

Our Architectural Philosophy:

  • • Multimodal Synergy: Fuse all 5 biosignals together (Brain + Eyes + Muscles + Heart + Breathing).
  • • Clinical Decision Gates:
    - rem_gate (EOG x EMG): Saccades x Muscle Atonia confirms REM.
    - apnea_gate (Resp x ECG): Airflow Drop x Heart Rate Surge.
    - obstructive_idx: Effort / Airflow (paradoxical breathing).
  • • Union Join Architecture: Preserve all 5,126 epochs with missingness flags (+25% data recovered; zero rows discarded).
  • • Robust Regularized ML: Calibrated LightGBM with per-subject Z-scoring that generalizes cleanly across unseen patients.
Philosophy: Clinical Logic + Data Hygiene Zero Data Loss
Pillar 4: Dataset Specifications

About the Dataset: PhysioNet PSG-IPA Profile

PhysioNet PSG-IPA v1.0.0 Profile:

  • • Gold-Standard Benchmark: 5 overnight hospital recordings (SN1 to SN5), totaling 5,126 thirty-second epochs (~42.7 hours at 256 Hz).
  • • 12 Expert Scorers (Superpower): Every single epoch was independently annotated by 12 certified clinical experts.
  • • Hard Consensus: Majority voting determines ground truth.
  • • Soft Labels: Captures medical ambiguity (e.g. 7 vote N2, 5 vote N1).
  • • Patient Cohort Nuances:
    - SN1: 901 ep (AHI 4.9, mild, balanced).
    - SN2: 730 ep (AHI 3.9, only 1 apnea epoch).
    - SN3: 1,640 ep (AHI 17.0, moderate-severe, 182 apnea ep).
    - SN4: 965 ep (AHI 4.1, elevated REM chin muscle activity).
    - SN5: 890 ep (AHI 13.2, 74% Wake outlier - severe insomnia).
5 Signals: EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, Resp/SaO2 12 Scorers
Pillar 5: Implementation Plan

Our Implementation Plan: 6-Stage End-to-End Pipeline

The 6-Stage Engineering Pipeline:

1. Signal Ingestion: MNE-Python reads raw 256 Hz streams. Dynamic channel resolver handles hardware variations (Cz-M1 vs C4-M1).
2. Digital Signal Processing: Zero-phase Butterworth filters (EEG 0.5-30Hz, EMG 10-100Hz, ECG 0.5-40Hz) + 50Hz notch filters.
3. 30s Windowing: Slicing continuous signals into 5,126 synchronized blocks (7,680 samples per epoch).
4. Feature Extraction: Computing Delta/Sigma powers, Spindle burst density, Saccades, and Wake-calibrated EMG Atonia.
5. Union Fusion: Merging 5 tables without row loss; injecting rem_gate, apnea_gate, and 90-min sleep cycles.
6. LOSO Validation: Train on 4 patients, test on 5th unseen patient across 5 folds with zero patient leakage.
Pillar 6: Experimental Benchmark

Verified Results: Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) Benchmark

Verified LOSO Metrics:

  • • Overall Accuracy: 61.7% across all 5 stages on unseen patients.
  • • Balanced Macro F1: 56.3% (Cohen's kappa = 0.485).
  • • Per-Stage Classification Highlights:
    - Stage N3 (Deep Sleep): 78.2% F1 (delta wave separation).
    - Stage N2 (Light Sleep): 68.1% F1 (spindle burst density).
    - Stage REM (Dreaming): 57.4% F1 (rem_gate saccade + atonia).
    - Stage Wake: 48.1% F1 (alpha rhythms and high chin tone).
    - Stage N1: 29.7% F1 (classic challenge, only ~6% prevalence).
  • • Individual Patients:
    - SN3 (Severe Apnea): F1 = 70.2% | kappa = 0.685
    - SN2 (Mild Apnea): F1 = 63.2% | kappa = 0.636
    - SN1 (Balanced): F1 = 59.3% | kappa = 0.581
Single Sensor: ~20% - 57% F1 Multimodal: 56.3% - 78.2% F1
Pillar 7: Advanced Foundation Models

Future Roadmap: Pathway to Human Expert Parity (kappa > 0.75)

Technique 1

Pretrained Meta-Features (YASA v0.7.0)

LightGBM trained on 30,000+ clinical nights.

How it bridges the gap: We extract YASA's zero-shot predicted probabilities as meta-features in our stacking ensemble, injecting 30,000 nights of clinical prior knowledge into our small cohort for free.
Zero-Shot Prior Knowledge
Technique 2

SleepFM Linear Probing (Stanford 2024)

Multimodal contrastive Transformer trained on 10,000+ nights of EEG, ECG, and Respiration.

How it bridges the gap: Freezing the SleepFM encoder and training a lightweight linear head on our 5 subjects circumvents the small-N overfitting ceiling completely (expected kappa = 0.72-0.76).
Overcomes Small Cohort Limits
Technique 3

Whole-Night Mamba (BiT-MamSleep)

Bidirectional Mamba State Space Sequence Model.

How it bridges the gap: Processes the entire 8-hour sleep recording (960 epochs) as a single sequence in linear O(L) time, natively learning the full night's ultradian sleep cycle without RNN gradient vanishing.
Linear O(L) Night Sequences
Executive Summary & Impact

Key Milestones & Clinical Impact

1. Multimodal Synergy

No Single Signal Can Diagnose Sleep Alone

EOG alone yielded ~57% F1 and EMG ~23%. Fusing Brain waves, Eye motion, Muscle tone, Heart rate, and Breathing creates a robust clinical picture and achieves 78.2% F1 in Deep Sleep (N3).

2. Data Hygiene

Data Quality Outperformed Model Complexity

Purging 17 dead zero-variance features and switching from inner join to Union Join recovered 1,032 discarded epochs (+25% data) and stabilized patient predictions across the cohort.

3. Clinical Logic

Clinical Rules Beat Black-Box Overfitting

Hardcoding medical decision rules (REM Saccades x Atonia, Respiratory Paradox) allowed regularized LightGBM to generalize cleanly across unseen patients without neural network collapse.

4. Future Roadmap

Roadmap to Human Expert Agreement (kappa > 0.75)

Incorporating pretrained sleep foundation models (SleepFM, trained on 10,000+ nights) and State Space Models (Mamba for whole-night O(L) context) bridges the final gap to human consensus.

Project Status: Phase 1-3 Verified | Ready for Foundation Model Fine-Tuning
